sources.title: Paul Hoffman, The Man Who Loved Only Numbers (1998) -- based on extensive interviews with Erdős's collaborators
Bruce Schechter, My Brain Is Open (1998)

achievement_drive.rationale: Documented lifetime output of approximately 1,525 mathematical papers, unsurpassed as of the most recent count -- a specific, independently verifiable bibliographic record, not a reputation claim.

collaboration.rationale: Documented 511 distinct co-authors across his career, the direct basis for the well-known 'Erdős number' phenomenon -- an unusually large, independently countable collaborative footprint.

curiosity.rationale: Documented as calculating, at age 5, the number of seconds a person had lived given their age, and being introduced to infinite series and set theory by his father at 16, proving Bertrand's postulate at 20 -- a specific, dated, escalating early-childhood pattern.

autonomy_need.rationale: Documented as never holding a permanent academic position, refusing a permanent offer from Notre Dame in 1952, and living out of a suitcase traveling continuously between collaborators for most of his adult life -- an unusual, sustained, well-documented lifestyle choice.

resourcefulness.rationale: Documented pattern of arriving at a collaborator's home expecting lodging, meals, laundry, and transportation to be arranged so he could work immediately -- inferred resourcefulness in sustaining a working, homeless-by-choice lifestyle for decades.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Documented sustained amphetamine and Ritalin use to extend working hours, including losing a $500 bet with Ron Graham that he could quit for a month, then resuming immediately afterward, remarking 'you've set mathematics back a month' -- a specific, dated, named-source incident scored dual-edged given the real health risk involved.

persistence.rationale: Documented as devoting waking hours to mathematics into his 80s, dying at a mathematics conference in Warsaw at age 83 rather than in retirement -- a sustained, lifelong pattern rather than a single incident.

impact_motivation.rationale: Documented as giving away most of the money he earned from lecturing and the $50,000 1983/84 Wolf Prize to help students or as problem-solving prize money -- inferred impact motivation over personal accumulation from this specific, sourced pattern.

creative_originality.rationale: Inferred from his documented invention of an entire private, idiosyncratic vocabulary for everyday concepts (children as 'epsilons', the US as 'Samland', God as the 'Supreme Fascist') -- a real, sourced, unusual pattern, though it speaks more to eccentricity than mathematical originality specifically, kept at moderate confidence.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Inferred from his documented practice of arriving unannounced at colleagues' homes and immediately directing the household toward supporting his work -- a real but narrow behavioral data point.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Documented as renouncing an honorary degree from the University of Waterloo shortly before his death specifically over its treatment of a colleague, Adrian Bondy -- a concrete, dated act of taking a costly stand on principle at the very end of his life.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Inferred from the documented breadth and depth of his output across number theory, combinatorics, graph theory, and set theory, corroborated by membership in scientific academies of at least 8 countries.

adaptability.rationale: Inferred from his documented navigation of a decade-long U.S. re-entry ban during McCarthyism (1954-1963), during which he worked from Israel instead, and resumed his prior working pattern once the visa was reinstated.

provenance.notes: Roster-17 intake (2026-09). Wikidata identity verified live (Q173746) before scoring. Evidence drawn from a live Wikipedia fetch, cross-referenced against the known Hoffman and Schechter biographies (both built on extensive named-collaborator interviews). Scored to 13 attributes this pass -- thinking-facet evidence beyond curiosity (analytical_rigor, systems_abstraction, intuitive_synthesis specifically) was not gathered with enough specificity this cycle to score defensibly, despite his obvious mathematical stature.

holdReason: Only 13 scored attributes (need 18); coverage 0.40 below the 0.6 threshold; 10 attributes at confidence>=0.5 (need 12). Exceptionally rich behavioral/eccentricity evidence already scored; this cycle's research did not surface strong enough sourcing on his specific mathematical thinking style (analytical_rigor, systems_abstraction, intuitive_synthesis) despite his obvious stature -- Hoffman's and Schechter's full biographies (only summarized here via the Wikipedia article) would very likely close this gap on a future pass.
